up: Create production raster sprite source cels for Battle of Gods, using the attached approved King anatomy/palette reference. One transparent PNG sprite sheet, EXACTLY 8 columns and 5 rows, forty fully separated complete body cels; equal cells, generous transparent margins, no labels, text, axes, guides, weapons, trails or background. All frames depict the SAME small chibi King: original charcoal tousled hair, compact round head, red scarf and trailing cloth, dark charcoal blue steel vest with light edges, warm brown gloves and boots, short native legs. Preserve the reference pixel art style and clear charcoal silhouette, no photorealism, no antialiasing gradients or lighting changes. SAME body/head size and pixel density in every cell; NO zooming and no huge spin body. Draw his whole connected head, neck/scarf, chest, both sleeved arms and hands, and both legs/boots in every cell. Hands CLOSED around an imagined axe shaft; DO NOT draw the axe itself, it is a separate rigid sprite attached later. Both shoulders and actual arms must connect to the torso. Intended 54-pixel-tall body after reduction, with large margins for arms. Each row is ONE continuous 8-cel attack: cels 1-2 anticipation, 3-6 cut/contact, 7-8 settling recovery. Row1 broad horizontal axe sweep across the FRONT of his physical body; row2 low-to-high rising cut; row3 high-to-low downward chop; row4 lift knees slightly to hop and forceful overhead slam, then grounded recovery; row5 circular waist-height whirlwind, clear fist motion around his body, then recover. Keep the viewer's camera angle identical throughout: RPG slightly top-down orthographic, whole body and boots visible. Clothes/head do NOT change and poses flow smoothly. Reference attachment shows side at left, UP/back at center, DOWN/front at right. DIRECTION for this entire sheet: UP/BACK. King faces AWAY from the viewer, attacking toward the top of the sheet. Show the BACK of his dark hair/head and back of his red neck scarf/steel vest, NEVER draw facial eyes. Keep scalp centered over the neck and body centered over the feet, no cut/floating head, no twisting into front view. Arms may reach to either side but each wrist is visibly connected. A little torso twist expresses momentum, always back-facing.
